attrs.definition: A pointer to a commit that moves forward as you work
A snapshot of your entire project at a point in time
Taking changes from one branch and applying them to another
A copy of your repo hosted somewhere else (GitHub, GitLab)
NVIDIA's parallel computing platform that lets you run code on the GPU
16-bit floating point, uses half the memory of fp32 with minimal accuracy loss
Specialized GPU cores for matrix multiplication, 4-8x faster than regular cores
Video RAM on the GPU, separate from system RAM. Limits model size.
A unique string that identifies your account and authorizes requests
Maximum requests per minute/hour to prevent abuse and ensure fair usage
Getting the response word by word instead of waiting for the full response
A billing unit: input and output tokens are counted and charged separately
An independently runnable unit in a notebook, either code or markdown
A JSON file containing cells, outputs, and metadata. Stands for IPython Notebook
A separate Python process that executes cells and keeps variables in memory
Special commands prefixed with % or %% that control the notebook environment
PyTorch was compiled for a different CUDA version than what your GPU driver supports
A file listing every package and its exact version, guaranteeing identical installs across machines
The standard Python project configuration file, replacing setup.py/setup.cfg/requirements.txt
Package B depends on C; if you install A which depends on B, C is a transitive dependency of A
An isolated directory containing a Python interpreter and packages, separate from the system Python
The FROM image your Dockerfile builds on top of. Determines what is pre-installed.
An isolated process using the host kernel, with its own filesystem and network
Each Dockerfile instruction creates a layer. Unchanged layers are cached, so rebuilds are fast.
A runtime hook that exposes host GPUs to containers via --gpus flag
A directory on the host mapped into the container. Changes persist after the container stops.
The editor runs a formatter (Black, Ruff) every time you save, so code style is always consistent
Language Server Protocol: a standard for editors to get type info, completions, and diagnostics from a language-specific server
Microsoft's Python language server using Pyright for type checking and IntelliSense
VS Code extension that runs a lightweight server on a remote machine and streams the UI to your local editor
An in-memory columnar format used internally by the datasets library for zero-copy reads
A local copy of previously fetched data, stored at ~/.cache/huggingface/ by default
A named subset (train/val/test) used at different stages of the ML lifecycle
A version control system for datasets and models that integrates with cloud storage
An extension that stores large files outside the git repo while keeping pointers in version control
A columnar file format optimized for analytical queries and storage efficiency
Processing data row by row from a remote source without downloading the full dataset
Runs a command immune to the hangup signal, so closing the terminal won't kill it
A unique number assigned to every running process, used to monitor or kill it
The | operator that sends one command's output as input to another
The program that interprets your commands (bash, zsh, fish)
Secure Shell, an encrypted protocol for running commands on a remote machine
A program that lets you run multiple terminal sessions inside one window, and detach/reattach
A minimal set of independent vectors that span the space
A measure of how aligned two vectors are -- the core of similarity search
A vector that represents the meaning of something (word, image, user)
No vector in the set can be written as a combination of the others
A transformation that maps vectors from one space to another
Vectors that are mutually perpendicular and each have length 1
The component of one vector in the direction of another
The number of linearly independent columns (or rows) in a matrix
A list of numbers representing a point or direction in n-dimensional space
Stretching a smaller array to match a larger one by repeating along missing dimensions.
Measures how much the matrix scales area (2D) or volume (3D). Zero means the transformation crushes a dimension.
Multiply matching positions. Both arrays must have the same shape (or be broadcastable).
The matrix equivalent of multiplying by 1. Used in residual connections (ResNets).
The matrix that reverses the transformation. Only exists when the determinant is not zero.
A linear transformation. It maps vectors from one space to another.
Dot products between every row of the first matrix and every column of the second. Order matters.
Swap rows and columns. Turns an m x n matrix into n x m. Critical in backpropagation.
An ordered list of numbers. In AI: a point in high-dimensional space.
det(A - lambda I) = 0. The polynomial whose roots are the eigenvalues.
Multiplying transformation matrices to chain operations. Order matters: B @ A means apply A first, then B.
The factor by which the transformation scales area (2D) or volume (3D). Zero means the transformation is irreversible.
Writing a matrix as V @ D @ V^(-1), separating it into its fundamental scaling directions and magnitudes.
The scalar factor by which the matrix scales its eigenvector. Can be negative (flip) or complex (rotation).
A direction that the matrix only scales, never rotates. The transformation's fingerprint.
A matrix that flips space across an axis or plane. Determinant is -1.
An orthogonal matrix that moves points along circular arcs while preserving distances and angles. Determinant is always 1.
A diagonal matrix that stretches or compresses independently along each axis. Determinant is the product of scale factors.
A matrix that shifts one coordinate proportionally to another, turning rectangles into parallelograms. Determinant is 1.
Computing gradients layer by layer from output to input using the chain rule. How neural networks learn.
The rule for differentiating composed functions: df/dx = df/dg dg/dx. The mathematical basis of backpropagation.
The rate of change of a function at a point. Tells you how much the output changes per unit change in input.
A vector of all partial derivatives. Points in the direction that increases the function fastest.
Subtract the gradient (times a learning rate) from the parameters to reduce the loss. The core of neural network training.
The matrix of all second-order partial derivatives. Describes the curvature of a function. Positive definite Hessian at a critical point means local minimum.
The accumulation of a quantity over a range. In ML, integrals define probabilities, expected values, and KL divergence.
When a function maps vectors to vectors, the Jacobian is the matrix of all partial derivatives of outputs with respect to inputs.
A scalar that controls how big each gradient descent step is. Too large: diverge. Too small: converge slowly.
Approximating a derivative by evaluating the function at two nearby points and computing the slope between them.
The derivative with respect to one variable while all others are held constant.
Approximating a function near a point using its derivatives: f(x+h) ~ f(x) + f'(x)h + (1/2)f''(x)h^2 + ... The basis for understanding why gradient descent and Newton's method work.
A system that records operations on values, builds a graph, and computes exact gradients via the chain rule
The derivative of composed functions equals the product of each function's local derivative, evaluated at the right point
A directed acyclic graph where nodes are operations and edges carry values (forward) or gradients (backward)
Numbers of the form a + bepsilon (epsilon^2 = 0) that carry derivative information through arithmetic
A computation graph rebuilt on every forward pass, allowing Python control flow inside models (PyTorch style)
Autodiff that propagates derivatives from inputs to outputs. One pass per input variable.
When a value feeds into multiple operations, its gradient is the sum of all incoming gradient contributions
Comparing autodiff gradients against numerical finite-difference gradients to verify correctness. Essential for debugging.
A neural network with one or more hidden layers of neurons. Each neuron computes a weighted sum plus bias, then applies an activation function.
The basic unit: output = activation(w1x1 + w2x2 + ... + b). The weights and bias are learnable parameters.
Autodiff that propagates gradients from outputs to inputs. One pass per output variable.
Ordering graph nodes so every node comes after all its dependencies. Required for correct gradient propagation.
The mean of many independent samples converges to a normal distribution regardless of the source
P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B). The foundation of Bayesian thinking and Bayes' theorem
-sum(p_true log(p_predicted)). Measures how different two distributions are. Lower is better
The probability-weighted sum of all outcomes. The loss function is an expected value
P(A and B) = P(A) P(B). Knowing one event tells you nothing about the other
P(X, Y) describes the probability of every combination of X and Y outcomes
log P(x). Turns products into sums, preventing numerical underflow in long sequences
Unnormalized scores before softmax. Named after the logistic function
P(X) = sum_y P(X, Y). Recovers one variable's distribution from the joint
f(x) = (1/sqrt(2pisigma^2)) exp(-(x-mu)^2/(2sigma^2)). Appears everywhere due to the CLT
A density function for continuous variables. Integrate it over an interval to get probability
A function that gives the exact probability of each discrete outcome, summing to 1
The set S of every possible outcome of an experiment
Generating values according to a probability distribution. How models generate output
softmax(z_i) = exp(z_i) / sum(exp(z_j)). Maps real-valued logits to a valid probability distribution
The expected squared deviation from the mean. High variance = noisy, unstable estimates
P(data) across all hypotheses. Ensures the posterior sums to 1.
The test says positive, but the true state is negative. Drives the base rate fallacy.
Adding a small count to every feature to prevent zero probabilities from unseen data.
P(evidence|hypothesis). How probable the observed data is under a specific hypothesis.
Using log(P) instead of P to avoid floating-point underflow when multiplying many small numbers.
Choose parameters that maximize P(data|parameters) P(parameters). Equivalent to regularized MLE.
Choose parameters that maximize P(data|parameters). No prior. Can overfit with small data.
A classifier that assumes features are independent given the class. Works well despite the false assumption.
P(hypothesis|evidence). The prior multiplied by the likelihood, then normalized.
P(hypothesis) before observing evidence. In ML: the regularization term.
Adaptive Moment Estimation. Tracks per-weight running averages of gradients and squared gradients to give each weight its own learning rate.
Adam's first and second moments are initialized to zero. Bias correction divides by (1 - beta^t) to compensate during early steps.
The optimizer has reached a point where further steps do not meaningfully reduce the loss.
A function where any local minimum is the global minimum. Gradient descent always finds it. Neural network losses are not convex.
Update weights by subtracting the gradient scaled by the learning rate. The most basic optimizer.
A scalar that controls how far each update moves the weights. Too large causes divergence. Too small wastes compute.
A function that adjusts the learning rate during training. Large steps early, small steps late.
The loss function plotted over weight space. Visualized by slicing along two random directions.
A small subset of training data (32-256 samples) used to estimate the gradient. Balances speed and gradient accuracy.
Accumulate past gradients into a velocity vector. Dampens oscillations and accelerates movement through consistent directions.
A point where the gradient is zero but it is a minimum in some directions and a maximum in others. Common in high dimensions.
Stochastic gradient descent. Compute gradient on a random subset instead of the full dataset. Almost always means mini-batch SGD in practice.
Information measured with log base 2. One bit resolves one fair coin flip.
Average surprise when using model distribution Q to encode events from true distribution P.
The average surprise across all outcomes of a distribution. Measures irreducible uncertainty.
The number of bits (or nats) needed to encode an event: -log(p)
Extra bits wasted by using Q instead of P. Equals cross-entropy minus entropy. Not symmetric.
Reduction in uncertainty about X from knowing Y. Zero means independent.
Information measured with natural log. Used by PyTorch and TensorFlow by default.
Identical to cross-entropy loss for one-hot labels. Minimizing it maximizes the probability of correct predictions.
Exponential of cross-entropy. The effective vocabulary size the model is choosing from at each step.
Exponentiate and normalize. Maps any real-valued vector to a valid probability distribution.
A symmetric matrix where entry (i,j) measures how feature i and feature j move together. Diagonal entries are individual variances.
Distances, volumes, and data density all behave counterintuitively as dimensions grow. Models need exponentially more data to compensate.
The fraction of total variance captured by one principal component. Sum the top k ratios to see how much k components preserve.
A lower-dimensional surface embedded in a higher-dimensional space. A sheet of paper crumpled in 3D is a 2D manifold.
Rotate your coordinate system so the axes align with the directions of maximum variance, then drop the low-variance axes.
Controls the effective number of neighbors each point considers. Low perplexity focuses on very local structure. High perplexity captures broader patterns.
An eigenvector of the covariance matrix. The direction in feature space along which the data varies most.
A nonlinear method that maps high-dimensional data to 2D by preserving pairwise neighborhood probabilities. Good for visualization, not for preprocessing.
A nonlinear method based on topological data analysis. Preserves both local and some global structure. Scales better than t-SNE.
sigma_max / sigma_min. A large condition number means small input changes cause large output changes. SVD reveals this directly.
For any target rank k, the truncated SVD minimizes the approximation error over all possible rank-k matrices.
Square root of the sum of squared entries. Equals the square root of the sum of squared singular values. Used to measure approximation error.
A dimension in the low-rank space discovered by SVD. In recommendations, a latent factor might correspond to genre preference. In NLP, it might correspond to a topic.
A column of U. The direction in output space that the i-th right singular vector maps to (after scaling by sigma_i).
Repeatedly multiply a random vector by the matrix and normalize. Converges to the eigenvector with the largest eigenvalue. The building block of many SVD algorithms.
V Sigma+ U^T. Inverts non-zero singular values, leaves zeros as zeros. Solves least-squares problems for non-square or singular matrices.
The number of non-zero singular values. Tells you how many independent directions the matrix actually uses.
A column of V. The direction in input space that the matrix maps to the i-th left singular vector (after scaling by sigma_i).
The i-th diagonal entry of Sigma. Measures how much the matrix stretches along the i-th principal direction. Always non-negative, sorted in decreasing order.
Decompose A into U Sigma V^T where U and V are orthogonal and Sigma is diagonal with non-negative entries. Works for any matrix of any shape.
Keep only the top k singular values and their vectors. Produces the provably best rank-k approximation to the original matrix (Eckart-Young theorem).
A strict set of rules: align from right, dimensions must be equal or one must be 1
Elements stored sequentially in memory with no gaps or reordering from the logical layout
The general operation where a shared index between tensors is multiplied and summed, producing a lower-rank result
A general notation that expresses any tensor contraction, outer product, trace, or transpose in one line
Memory layout conventions for image tensors. NCHW puts channels before spatial dims, NHWC puts them after
The number of axes. A matrix has rank 2, not rank equal to its matrix rank
A tuple listing the size along each axis. (2, 3) means 2 rows, 3 columns
The number of elements to skip to advance one position along each axis
A multi-dimensional array with uniform type and defined shape, strides, and operations
A tensor sharing the same memory buffer but with different shape/stride metadata. Fails on non-contiguous data
Google's 16-bit format with 8 exponent bits (same range as float32) and 7 mantissa bits (less precision than float16). Preferred for training.
When subtracting nearly equal floating point numbers, significant digits cancel and rounding noise dominates the result.
Comparing analytical gradients from backpropagation against numerical gradients from finite differences to catch implementation bugs.
Scaling the gradient vector so its norm does not exceed a threshold. Prevents exploding gradients from ruining weights.
International standard defining binary floating point formats, rounding rules, and special values (inf, nan). Every modern CPU and GPU implements it.
Special float value from overflow or division by zero. Can combine to produce NaN (inf - inf, inf 0).
Computing log(sum(exp(x))) by factoring out exp(max(x)) to prevent overflow and underflow. Used in softmax, cross-entropy, and log-probability math.
Multiplying the loss by a large constant before backprop so gradients stay in float16's representable range, then dividing by the same constant before weight updates.
The smallest value e such that 1.0 + e != 1.0 in a given float format. For float32, it is about 1.19e-7.
Using lower-precision floats for speed-critical operations and higher-precision floats for numerically sensitive operations. Typical speedup is 2-3x.
Special float value from undefined operations (0/0, inf-inf, sqrt(-1)). Propagates through all subsequent arithmetic.
Approximating a derivative by evaluating f(x+h) and f(x-h) and dividing by 2h. Slow but reliable for verification.
A result exceeds the maximum representable value and becomes inf. exp(89) overflows float32.
Subtracting max(logits) before exponentiating. Numerically identical result, no overflow possible.
A result is closer to zero than the smallest representable positive number and becomes 0.0. exp(-104) underflows float32.
Algorithms (HNSW, LSH, IVF) that find approximately closest points much faster than exact search
Converts cosine similarity to a distance. Ranges from 0 to 2
Dot product normalized by both magnitudes. Ranges from -1 to +1. Ignores vector length
Sum of component-wise products. Equals cosine similarity times both magnitudes
Minimum insertions, deletions, and substitutions to transform one string into another
Combines L1 and L2 regularization. Handles correlated feature groups better than either alone
Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph. Multi-layer graph for fast approximate nearest neighbor search
Size of intersection divided by size of union. For sets, not vectors
Not a true distance (not symmetric). Measures extra bits from using Q to encode P
The maximum absolute component value. The limit of Lp as p approaches infinity
Sum of absolute component values. Produces sparsity in optimization. Robust to outliers
Adding the L1 norm of weights to the loss. Drives weights to zero (sparsity)
Square root of sum of squared components. The straight-line distance in Euclidean space
Adding the squared L2 norm of weights to the loss. Shrinks weights toward zero without sparsity
The p-th root of the sum of p-th powers of absolute components. L1 and L2 are special cases
L2 distance in a space that has been whitened (decorrelated and normalized) using the data covariance matrix
A function that maps a vector to a non-negative scalar, satisfying triangle inequality, absolute homogeneity, and zero only for the zero vector
Minimum work to transport mass from one distribution to another. A true metric
Divides significance threshold by number of tests to control false positives.
Resampling with replacement to estimate sampling distributions.
Sample means converge to a normal distribution as sample size grows.
Tests whether observed frequencies differ from expected frequencies.
Range of plausible values for a parameter at a given confidence level.
Matrix of pairwise covariances between all features.
Magnitude of a difference, independent of sample size. Cohen's d is common.
Interquartile range. Q3 minus Q1. The spread of the middle 50%.
Sum of values divided by count. Sensitive to outliers.
Middle value of sorted data. Robust to outliers.
Makes no distributional assumptions. Works on ranks or signs.
Default assumption of no effect or no difference.
Probability of data this extreme given the null hypothesis is true.
Assumes a specific distribution for the data (usually normal).
Measures linear association between two variables. Range [-1, 1].
Value below which a given percentage of data falls.
Measures monotonic association using ranks.
Square root of variance. Measures spread in original units.
Probability of correctly rejecting a false H0. Power = 1 minus Type II error rate.
Tests whether means differ significantly. Uses the t-distribution.
False positive. Rejecting H0 when it is true.
False negative. Failing to reject H0 when it is false.
Initial MCMC samples discarded before the chain reaches its stationary distribution
p(x) T(x->y) = p(y) T(y->x). Sufficient condition for p to be the stationary distribution of a Markov chain
Generate data by starting from noise and applying learned denoising steps. Each step is a conditional sampling operation
Update each variable from its conditional distribution holding others fixed. 100% acceptance rate
Differentiable approximation to categorical sampling using Gumbel noise + softmax with temperature
Estimate expectations under p(x) using samples from q(x) by weighting each sample by p(x)/q(x). Core to PPO in RL
F_inverse(U) converts a uniform sample into a sample from any distribution with known CDF. Exact and efficient
Construct a Markov chain whose stationary distribution is the target. Metropolis-Hastings is the foundational algorithm
Propose moves, accept based on density ratio. Detailed balance ensures convergence to target distribution
Approximate integrals as sample averages. Error O(1/sqrt(N)) regardless of dimension
Keep the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p. Adaptive candidate set size
Generate from a simple proposal, accept with probability proportional to target/proposal ratio. Exact but wastes samples
Write z = mu + sigma epsilon where epsilon ~ N(0,1). Makes sampling differentiable. Essential for VAE training
Generating values according to a probability distribution. The mechanism behind all generative AI
Divide sample space into strata, sample from each. Always lower variance than naive Monte Carlo
Divides logits by T before softmax. T<1 sharpens (more confident), T>1 flattens (more diverse)
Zero out all but the k highest-probability tokens, renormalize, sample. Fixed candidate set size
Every value in [a, b] has equal probability density 1/(b-a). The starting point for all sampling methods
Given an upper triangular system, solve the last equation first, then substitute backward. O(n^2).
For symmetric positive definite A, write A = LL^T. Half the cost of LU. Used for covariance matrices, kernel matrices, and ridge regression.
kappa = sigma_max / sigma_min. Measures sensitivity to input perturbations. Lose about log10(kappa) digits of precision.
An iterative solver for symmetric positive definite systems. Converges in at most n steps. Practical for large sparse systems where factorization is too expensive.
Given a lower triangular system, solve the first equation first, then substitute forward. O(n^2). Used in the L step of LU solves.
Systematically zero out entries below the diagonal using row operations, producing an upper triangular system solvable by back substitution. O(n^3).
^2 when the system is overdetermined (more equations than unknowns).
A set of linear equations Ax = b. Finding x means finding the input that produces output b under transformation A.
Write A = LU where L is lower triangular (stores multipliers) and U is upper triangular (the eliminated matrix). Amortizes the O(n^3) cost over multiple solves.
^2 to zero. This IS the closed-form solution to linear regression.
m > n in an m-by-n system. No exact solution exists. Least squares finds the best approximation. This is every regression problem.
Before eliminating in column k, swap the row with the largest absolute value in that column to the pivot position. Prevents division by small numbers.
A+ = V Sigma+ U^T via SVD. Gives the minimum-norm least-squares solution for any matrix, square or rectangular, singular or not.
Write A = QR where Q has orthonormal columns and R is upper triangular. More stable than LU for least squares.
Solve (X^T X + lambda I) w = X^T y. Adding lambda I improves conditioning and shrinks weights toward zero. Prevents overfitting.
At the solution, either a constraint is active or its multiplier is zero. Never both nonzero
Ratio of largest to smallest eigenvalue of the Hessian. High condition number means elongated valleys and slow gradient descent
A function where the line between any two points on its graph lies above or on the graph. Equivalently, Hessian is positive semidefinite everywhere
A set where the line segment between any two points in the set stays inside the set
Every constrained problem has a companion dual problem. For convex problems, both have the same optimal value
The lowest point of a function over its entire domain
The matrix of all second partial derivatives. Encodes curvature information
Necessary conditions for optimality with inequality constraints. Generalize Lagrange multipliers
Approximate second-order method that stores the last m gradient differences instead of the full Hessian
A variable introduced to convert a constrained optimization problem into an unconstrained one
A point lower than all nearby points. For convex functions, every local minimum is the global minimum
Second-order optimizer that uses the inverse Hessian to determine step direction and size. Quadratic convergence near the minimum
Using more parameters than training examples. Smooths the loss landscape and reduces bad local minima
A matrix whose eigenvalues are all non-negative. The multidimensional analogue of "second derivative >= 0"
A point where the gradient is zero but it is a minimum in some directions and a maximum in others
Primal and dual optimal values are equal. Holds for convex problems satisfying Slater's condition
A number a + bi where a is the real part, b is the imaginary part, and i^2 = -1
The 2D plane where the x-axis is real and the y-axis is imaginary. Also called the Argand plane
The mirror image across the real axis: conjugate of a + bi is a - bi
Discrete Fourier Transform. Decomposes a signal into complex sinusoidal components using roots of unity
e^(itheta) = cos(theta) + isin(theta). Connects exponentials to trigonometry
The number i, defined by i^2 = -1. Not imaginary in the philosophical sense -- it is a rotation operator
The distance from the origin: sqrt(a^2 + b^2). Written as |z|
The angle from the positive real axis: atan2(b, a). Written as arg(z)
A rotating complex number e^(iomegat) representing a sinusoidal signal
Expressing z as r e^(itheta) instead of a + bi. Makes multiplication easy
The N complex numbers e^(2piik/N) for k = 0 to N-1. N equally spaced points on the unit circle
Rotary Position Embedding. Uses complex multiplication to encode relative position in transformer attention
When frequencies above Nyquist appear as lower frequencies due to insufficient sampling rate
Convolution where the signal wraps around. This is what the DFT naturally computes
Convolution in time domain equals pointwise multiplication in frequency domain. Fundamental to signal processing and CNNs
X[0], the zero-frequency coefficient. Proportional to the signal mean
Converts N time-domain samples into N frequency-domain coefficients. Each coefficient is the correlation with a complex sinusoid at that frequency
An O(N log N) algorithm to compute the DFT. The Cooley-Tukey algorithm splits even/odd indices recursively
Each index k in the DFT output represents frequency kfs/N Hz. The "bin" is the discrete frequency slot
Reconstructs the time-domain signal from frequency coefficients. Same formula as DFT with flipped exponent sign and 1/N scaling
Standard convolution without wraparound. Achieved by zero-padding before DFT
fs/2, the maximum frequency representable at sampling rate fs. Frequencies above this alias
Total energy is preserved through the Fourier transform. sum |x[n]|^2 = (1/N) sum |X[k]|^2
angle(X[k]), the phase offset of each frequency component. Often ignored in analysis
|X[k]|^2, the squared magnitude of each frequency coefficient. Shows energy distribution across frequencies
Spurious frequency content caused by treating a non-periodic signal as periodic. Reduced by windowing
The complex exponential e^(-2piik/N) used to combine sub-DFTs in the FFT butterfly computation
A tapering function (Hann, Hamming, Blackman) applied before DFT to reduce spectral leakage
An n x n matrix where A[i][j] = 1 if nodes i and j are connected
Traversal that visits all neighbors before going deeper, finds shortest paths
A maximal subgraph where every node can reach every other node
The number of edges touching a node
Traversal that follows one path to its end before backtracking
The smallest non-zero eigenvalue of L, measuring how well-connected the graph is
A mathematical structure G=(V,E) encoding pairwise relationships
L = D - A, the matrix whose eigenvalues reveal graph structure
Each node aggregates information from its neighbors, the core of GNNs
Partition a graph using eigenvectors of its Laplacian
The continuous-time limit of a random walk, B(t) ~ N(0, t)
Forward: gradually add noise. Reverse: gradually remove it. Generates data.
Update rule that combines deterministic gradient and random perturbation
The future depends only on the present state, not on the history
Constructing a Markov chain whose stationary distribution is the one you want
MCMC algorithm that uses acceptance ratios to ensure convergence
A process where position changes by random increments at each step
The distribution pi where piP = pi -- the chain's equilibrium
Parameter controlling the tradeoff between exploration and exploitation
P[i][j] = probability of moving from state i to state j
Repeatedly splitting data into train/test folds and averaging results, giving a more robust performance estimate
The statistical distribution of incoming data shifts over time, degrading model performance
A measurable property of the data that the model uses to make predictions
The model's ability to make accurate predictions on data it was not trained on
A parameter set before training that controls the learning process (learning rate, number of layers)
The known output for a training example, used to compute the error signal
A function that measures the gap between predicted and actual outputs, which training tries to minimize
A mathematical function with learnable parameters that maps inputs to outputs
The model learned training-specific noise instead of general patterns, so it fails on new data
Adding a penalty term to the loss function that discourages overly complex models
Running an optimization algorithm to adjust model parameters so predictions match known outputs
The model is too simple to capture the real patterns in the data
A function that maps model parameters to a single number measuring prediction error, which optimization minimizes
Transforming features to similar ranges (e.g., zero mean, unit variance) so gradient descent converges faster
Iteratively adjust parameters in the direction that reduces the cost function, using partial derivatives
A scalar that controls how much parameters change per gradient descent step
Find weight w and bias b that minimize the sum of squared differences between wx+b and actual y values
(1/n) sum of (predicted - actual)^2, penalizing large errors disproportionately
The closed-form solution w = (X^T X)^-1 X^T y that gives optimal weights without iteration
Using a model so complex that it fits noise in training data and fails on new data
Linear regression on polynomial features (x, x^2, x^3, ...), still linear in the weights
The fraction of variance in y explained by the model, ranging from negative infinity to 1.0
Adding a term to the cost function that shrinks weights, preventing overfitting
Linear regression with a penalty of lambda sum(w_i^2) added to MSE
The loss function -[ylog(p) + (1-y)log(1-p)] that penalizes confident wrong predictions severely
The extension of binary cross-entropy to k classes using one-hot encoded labels
A table showing TP, TN, FP, FN counts for each class pair
The surface where the model's output probability equals 0.5, separating predicted classes
The harmonic mean of precision and recall: 2PR / (P+R)
A linear model followed by a sigmoid function that outputs class probabilities
Representing class k as a vector of zeros with a 1 at position k
TP / (TP + FP), the fraction of positive predictions that are actually positive
TP / (TP + FN), the fraction of actual positives that the model correctly identifies
The function 1/(1+e^(-z)) that maps any real number to the range (0, 1)
A function that converts a vector of scores into probabilities that sum to 1
The probability value above which the model predicts class 1 (default 0.5, tunable)
Bootstrap aggregating. Train each model on a different random sample with replacement
A random sample drawn with replacement from the original dataset. Same size, but with duplicates
A model that partitions feature space into rectangular regions by learning a sequence of if/else splits
Information content at a node. 0 = pure, 1.0 = maximum uncertainty for binary. From information theory
Total impurity decrease contributed by each feature, summed across all trees and nodes
Probability of misclassifying a random sample at a node. 0 = pure, 0.5 = maximum impurity for binary
Reduction in impurity after a split. The greedy criterion for choosing splits
Accuracy drop when a feature's values are randomly shuffled. More reliable than MDI for noisy features
Growing the full tree, then removing subtrees that do not improve validation performance
Stopping tree growth early by setting max depth, min samples, or min gain thresholds
Ensemble of decision trees, each trained on a bootstrap sample with random feature subsets at each split
The regression tree analogue of information gain. Picks the split that reduces target variance the most
Trade-off between margin width and classification errors. Large C = narrow margin, small C = wide margin
Reformulation of the SVM problem that depends only on dot products between data points. Enables kernels
max(0, 1 - yf(x)). Zero when correctly classified and outside the margin. Linear penalty otherwise
Computing dot products in a high-dimensional feature space without explicitly mapping to that space
K(x, z) = x . z. Equivalent to standard dot product. For linearly separable data
The distance between the decision boundary and the nearest support vectors. SVMs maximize this
The principle of choosing the hyperplane that maximizes the distance to the nearest points of each class
K(x, z) = (x . z + c)^d. Maps to a feature space of polynomial combinations
K(x, z) = exp(-gamma ||x-z||^2). Maps to infinite dimensions. Learns any smooth boundary
xi_i: measures how much a point violates the margin. Zero for correctly classified points outside margin
SVM formulation that allows margin violations via slack variables. Handles non-separable data
The training points closest to the decision boundary. The only points that determine the hyperplane
Support Vector Regression. Fits an epsilon-tube around the data. Points inside the tube have zero loss
Algorithms (HNSW, LSH, IVF) that find approximately nearest points much faster than exact search
Tree of nested hyperspheres. Works better than KD-trees in moderate dimensions (up to ~50)
Computing distance to every training point. O(nd) per query. Exact but slow for large n
In high dimensions, distances converge and neighborhoods expand to cover most of the space, making KNN ineffective
Heavy computation at training time to build a compact model. Most ML algorithms are eager
Normalizing features to comparable ranges. Required for distance-based methods like KNN
Non-parametric algorithm that predicts by finding the K closest training points to a query
Binary tree that recursively partitions space along feature axes. O(log n) queries in low dimensions
No computation at training time. All work happens at prediction time. KNN is the canonical example
Classification by counting which class is most common among K neighbors
The partition of space where each region contains all points closer to one training point than any other. K=1 KNN produces Voronoi boundaries
Neighbors weighted inversely by distance. Closer neighbors have more influence on the prediction
A data point that does not conform to the expected pattern, identified as noise by DBSCAN or low-probability by GMM
The mean of all points assigned to a cluster; used by K-Means as the cluster representative
Partitioning data into subsets where within-group similarity exceeds between-group similarity, measured by a specific distance metric
A point with at least min_samples neighbors within eps distance, in DBSCAN
A tree diagram showing the order and distance at which clusters were merged in hierarchical clustering
Expectation-Maximization: iteratively compute membership probabilities (E-step) and update distribution parameters (M-step)
Sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned centroid; lower is tighter
For each point, (b - a) / max(a, b) where a is mean intra-cluster distance and b is mean nearest-cluster distance
Using information during training that would not be available at prediction time, giving falsely optimistic results
Transforming raw data into representations that expose patterns to the model
Removing features that add noise or redundancy, keeping only those with signal about the target
Replacing missing values with estimated values (mean, median, mode, or model-predicted)
A measure of the reduction in uncertainty about variable Y gained by observing variable X
attrs.folk_definition: "How much one thing tells you about another"

attrs.definition: Creating one binary column per category, where exactly one column is 1 for each row
Subtracting the mean and dividing by standard deviation so the feature has mean=0 and std=1
Replacing each category with the average target value for that category, with smoothing to prevent overfitting
Term Frequency times Inverse Document Frequency: words weighted by how distinctive they are across the corpus
The area under the curve of true positive rate vs false positive rate across all thresholds, from 0.5 (random) to 1.0 (perfect)
Systematically rotating which portion of data is used for validation, averaging results across all rotations
Using information during training that would not be available at prediction time, leading to optimistic evaluation
A plot of training and validation scores vs training set size, revealing underfitting or overfitting
The model captures noise in the training data, performing well on training but poorly on unseen data
TP / (TP + FP): the fraction of positive predictions that are actually positive
1 - (sum of squared residuals / total sum of squares): the fraction of target variance captured by the model
TP / (TP + FN): the fraction of actual positives that were correctly identified
Splitting data so each subset has the same proportion of each class as the full dataset
Systematic error from wrong assumptions. The gap between the average model prediction and truth.
Test error decreases again when model capacity far exceeds the interpolation threshold.
Error from randomness in the true data-generating process. No model can eliminate it.
The capacity of a model to fit arbitrary patterns. Controlled by architecture, features, or regularization.
Model has high variance. It fits noise in training data that does not generalize.
Adding a penalty to reduce model complexity, trading bias for lower variance.
Model has high bias. It misses the real pattern even on training data.
Error from sensitivity to training data. How much predictions change across different training sets.
Boosting via sample weight updates; misclassified points get higher weight for the next learner
Bootstrap aggregating: train models on bootstrap samples, average predictions to reduce variance
Train models sequentially, each correcting errors of the ensemble so far, to reduce bias
Models must be uncorrelated in their errors for the ensemble to improve over individuals
Boosting via fitting each new model to the negative gradient of the loss function
Samples not in a bootstrap draw (~36.8%) serve as a validation set without needing a holdout
Bagging with decision trees, adding random feature subsampling at each split for diversity
Use predictions of base models as input features for a meta-learner
Gradient boosting with regularization, second-order optimization, and systems-level speed tricks
Scores candidate points by balancing expected improvement with uncertainty. EI and UCB are common choices.
Uses a surrogate model of the objective to decide where to evaluate next, balancing exploration and exploitation
Terminate training early when validation performance stops improving
Exhaustive search over a specified parameter grid. Exponential cost.
Adaptive resource allocation: start many configs with small budgets, keep the best and increase their budgets
A value set before training that controls the learning process, not learned from data
A function that adjusts the learning rate over the course of training for better convergence
Sample hyperparameters from distributions. Covers important dimensions better than grid search.
A model (usually Gaussian process) that approximates the expensive objective function from observed evaluations
Applies different pipelines to different subsets of columns, combining results
Using information from outside the training set to build the model, inflating performance estimates
Version control system for large data files, storing hashes in git and data in remote storage
Recording parameters, metrics, artifacts, and code versions for every training run
Open-source platform for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment
A system that tracks model versions with stage labels (staging, production, archived)
An ordered sequence of fitted transformers and a model, applied as one unit to prevent leakage
The ability to get identical results from the same code, data, and configuration
Differences between how data is processed during training versus inference, causing silent errors
P(A, B | C) = P(A | C) P(B | C) -- knowing B tells you nothing new about A once you know C
A model that directly learns P(Y | X) without modeling how X is generated
A model that learns P(X | Y) and P(Y), then uses Bayes' theorem to get P(Y | X)
Adding a small count to every feature to prevent zero probabilities from dominating the prediction
P(features | class) -- the probability of observing these features if the class is known
Working with log P instead of P to prevent the product of many small numbers from becoming zero in floating point
A classifier that applies Bayes' theorem with the assumption that features are conditionally independent given the class
P(class | features) -- the updated probability of the class after observing the features
P(class) -- the probability of each class before observing any features
AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average: combines past values (AR), differencing (I), and past errors (MA)
The correlation between a time series and a lagged copy of itself, as a function of the lag
Computing y[t] - y[t-1] to remove trends and achieve stationarity
Walk-forward validation where the training set grows with each fold
Using y[t-1], y[t-2], ..., y[t-k] as features to predict y[t]
Autocorrelation at lag k after removing the effect of all shorter lags
Regular, predictable cycles in a time series tied to calendar periods (daily, weekly, yearly)
Walk-forward validation where the training set is a fixed-length window that slides forward
A series whose mean, variance, and autocorrelation structure are constant over time
A persistent increase or decrease in the series level over time
Evaluation where training data always precedes test data chronologically
A data point that deviates significantly from the expected pattern of normal data
A metric that summarizes precision-recall performance across all thresholds, better than AUROC for imbalanced data
A hyperparameter telling the detector what proportion of the data it should flag as anomalous
An observation that is unusual given its context (time, location, etc.) but might be normal in another context
Q3 - Q1, measuring the spread of the middle 50% of data, used for robust outlier detection
An ensemble of random trees that isolates anomalies with fewer splits than normal points
A method that flags points whose local density is much lower than their neighbors' density
An individual observation that is unusual regardless of context
Precision computed on only the k most suspicious points, useful for imbalanced anomaly detection
attrs.folk_definition: "Of the top k flags, how many are real"

attrs.definition: (x - mean) / std, measuring how far a point is from the center in units of standard deviation
Summarizes the precision-recall curve into a single number; more informative than AUC-ROC when classes are heavily imbalanced
The distribution of classes in the dataset is significantly skewed, causing models to favor the majority class
Multiplying the loss function by class-specific weights so the model penalizes minority misclassification more heavily
attrs.folk_definition: "Making errors on rare classes more expensive"

attrs.definition: Incorporating real-world misclassification costs into the training objective so the model optimizes for total cost, not error count
A correlation between predicted and actual labels that produces a high score only when the model performs well on both classes
Lowering the threshold catches more positives (higher recall) but also flags more false positives (lower precision), and vice versa
Repeating minority class samples to balance class counts; simple but risks overfitting to duplicated points

attrs.in_practice: Normalize content, use exact hashes and similarity methods, review borderline clusters, and record which version and rule removed each example.
attrs.name: Data Deduplication
attrs.why_it_matters: Repetition can distort the training distribution, increase memorization, leak test material, and make evaluation appear stronger than it is.

attrs.definition: The statistical distribution of incoming data shifts over time, degrading model performance

attrs.confusion: Exfiltration is about unauthorized movement or disclosure. Ordinary retrieval of data by an authorized component is not exfiltration, although later use can become one.
attrs.definition: Unauthorized transfer of protected data from a system or trust zone to a person, tool, service, or storage location that is not permitted to receive it.
attrs.in_practice: Minimize readable data, allowlist destinations, inspect outbound tool calls, redact sensitive fields, and alert on unusual transfers across trust boundaries.
attrs.name: Data Exfiltration
attrs.why_it_matters: An agent can expose secrets through generated text, tool arguments, URLs, logs, or side effects even when the original data store remains intact.

attrs.confusion: Leakage is not limited to duplicate rows. Global normalization statistics, timestamps, target-derived features, and repeated test-driven prompt edits can all leak information.
attrs.definition: Unintended use of information during training or feature construction that would not be available at the real prediction point or belongs to a held-out evaluation boundary.
attrs.in_practice: Split data before fitting preprocessors, keep future information out of historical features, and isolate test labels and benchmark answers from prompts and tuning loops.
attrs.name: Data Leakage
attrs.why_it_matters: Leakage produces optimistic metrics that collapse when the system encounters genuinely unseen inputs.

attrs.confusion: Data provenance explains origin and custody broadly. Lineage emphasizes the transformation path and dependencies between data artifacts.
attrs.definition: A record of how a data artifact was derived across sources, transformations, joins, filters, versions, and downstream uses.
attrs.in_practice: Give inputs and outputs stable identifiers, record each transformation and version, preserve parent-child relationships, and test whether an affected source can be traced to every derivative.
attrs.name: Data Lineage
attrs.why_it_matters: When a source is corrected, revoked, or found unsafe, lineage identifies which datasets, embeddings, evaluations, and model artifacts may be affected.

attrs.confusion: Minimization does not mean keeping no data. It means being able to justify each data element, use, recipient, and retention period against the stated purpose.
attrs.definition: For personal data, limiting what is collected, processed, exposed, and retained to what is necessary for a specified purpose. Teams can apply the same discipline to sensitive non-personal data as an engineering control.
attrs.in_practice: Define the required fields before collection, redact or aggregate at the earliest boundary, set retention limits, and verify that optional context improves a measured task outcome before keeping it.
attrs.name: Data Minimization
attrs.why_it_matters: Every unnecessary field placed in a prompt, trace, cache, or tool call increases privacy exposure and the possible impact of misuse or compromise.

attrs.in_practice: Assign immutable dataset versions, record transformation jobs and source identifiers, and carry lineage metadata into embeddings, eval cases, and model artifacts.

attrs.why_it_matters: A dataset is not safe or suitable merely because it is available. Downstream builders need evidence about how it was created and where its assumptions break.

attrs.definition: Multimodal model reads figures and rewrites them for clarity
attrs.name: Vision-language critique

attrs.confusion: Accepting an image does not prove the model uses it correctly, and a VLM is not necessarily able to generate images.
attrs.definition: A model that learns relationships between, or jointly processes, visual and language representations for tasks such as retrieval, description, question answering, or grounded generation.
attrs.in_practice: Evaluate text-only and vision-only controls, vary image resolution and layout, require evidence localization where possible, and report failures by visual skill and language.
attrs.name: Vision-Language Model (VLM)
attrs.why_it_matters: VLM performance depends on the visual encoder, language component, connection mechanism, training data, and resolution policy rather than one generic capability label.

attrs.confusion: ViT is an architecture family, not every transformer that accepts images, and its patches are not inherently semantic objects.
attrs.definition: A vision architecture that represents an image as a sequence of patch embeddings with position information and processes that sequence with transformer encoder blocks.
attrs.in_practice: Keep patching and normalization consistent with training, account for position-embedding behavior at new resolutions, and compare against a suitable visual baseline on the target dataset.
attrs.name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
attrs.why_it_matters: It provides a sequence-model interface for visual data, but performance and compute depend on patch size, resolution, pretraining, and inductive biases.

attrs.definition: VLM operating GUIs (OSWorld, mobile, web) with tool calls
attrs.name: Visual agent

attrs.confusion: Visual grounding identifies where the referenced evidence is. General image captioning can describe a scene without localizing each claim.
attrs.definition: Connecting a language expression to spatial evidence in an image or video, such as a region, object, mask, or tracked entity.
attrs.in_practice: Require a box, mask, or temporal segment with the answer, test ambiguous and absent referents, and score localization separately from language correctness.
attrs.name: Visual Grounding
attrs.why_it_matters: A fluent visual answer can be unsupported, while grounding makes the claimed referent inspectable and enables region-level evaluation.

attrs.definition: Training on GPT-4-generated (image, instruction, response) triplets
attrs.name: Visual instruction tuning

attrs.definition: Rough count of patch tokens emitted per image; sets the LLM's prompt budget and attention cost

attrs.definition: Agent calls external vision tools (OCR, detection) mid-plan

attrs.definition: 2024 benchmark for end-to-end web tasks
attrs.name: VisualWebArena

attrs.definition: The canonical size: dim=768, depth=12, heads=12, patch_size=16, image=224; ~86M params
attrs.name: ViT-B/16

attrs.definition: Vision encoder + projector + language model; every 2026 VLM
attrs.name: ViT-MLP-LLM

attrs.definition: Benchmark for model's ability to read non-semantic visual encoding

attrs.definition: Finds the highest-probability tag sequence given emissions and transitions.

attrs.definition: Model that takes image + instruction and outputs action commands

attrs.definition: Broad production baseline 2026

attrs.confusion: A model vocabulary is not a dictionary of human words; many entries are fragments, bytes, whitespace patterns, or control symbols.
attrs.definition: The finite mapping between token identifiers and the units a tokenizer can emit, including ordinary, byte-level, and special control tokens.
attrs.in_practice: Version the vocabulary and special-token assignments with the model, test encode-decode round trips, and never substitute a tokenizer with merely similar token names.
attrs.name: Vocabulary
attrs.why_it_matters: Vocabulary design affects sequence length, multilingual coverage, code representation, embedding size, and compatibility between tokenizers and model weights.

attrs.definition: The total number of unique tokens: GPT-2 has 50,257, BERT has 30,522, Llama 3 has 128,256
attrs.name: Vocabulary size

attrs.definition: Neural net mapping mel-spec to raw samples.
attrs.name: Vocoder

attrs.definition: Gate that removes silence before ASR; cuts cost massively.
attrs.name: Voice activity detection

attrs.definition: Model ingests speech and emits speech without text detour.
attrs.name: Voice-in / voice-out

attrs.definition: Speaker embedding or token prefix that steers the cloned voice.
attrs.name: Voice prompt

attrs.definition: STT + LLM + TTS; text-level control
attrs.name: VoicePipelineAgent

attrs.definition: A directory on the host mapped into the container. Changes persist after the container stops.
attrs.name: Volume mount

attrs.definition: Composite samples along a ray into a single pixel using transmittance and alpha
attrs.name: Volumetric rendering

attrs.definition: AgentVerse emergent pattern: an agent offers to take a step.
attrs.name: Volunteer behavior

attrs.definition: The partition of space where each region contains all points closer to one training point than any other. K=1 KNN produces Voronoi boundaries
attrs.name: Voronoi diagram

attrs.definition: The simplest parallel inference topology; useful for classification, less for long-form reasoning
attrs.name: Voting ensemble

attrs.definition: Vector-quantized tokens that decode cleanly back to pixels
attrs.name: VQ for generation

attrs.definition: Replace continuous z with nearest codebook vector; enables transformer modelling.
attrs.name: VQ-VAE

attrs.definition: Task of answering a free-form question about an image
attrs.name: VQA

attrs.definition: Video RAM on the GPU, separate from system RAM. Limits model size.
attrs.name: VRAM

attrs.definition: (d_model, d_model) matrix applied after concatenating heads; where heads mix.
attrs.name: W_o

attrs.definition: Output of the mapping network; roughly disentangled.
attrs.name: W space

attrs.definition: Fine-tuning a strong model on weak labels and measuring the capability recovered
attrs.name: W2SG

attrs.definition: Parent span propagates into CLI subprocess
attrs.name: W3C trace context

attrs.definition: Short keyword detector; Porcupine, Snowboy, openWakeWord.
attrs.name: Wake word

attrs.definition: Evaluation where training data always precedes test data chronologically
attrs.name: Walk-forward validation

attrs.definition: min_workers >= 1 to keep at least one replica ready
attrs.name: Warm pool

attrs.confusion: Warmup is not required for every model and does not make an otherwise unsuitable learning rate safe.
attrs.definition: An initial training phase in which the learning rate rises from a smaller value toward the main schedule's target value.
attrs.in_practice: Define warmup in steps or processed tokens, log the realized curve, and tune it with the batch, optimizer, and total training budget held visible.
attrs.name: Warmup
attrs.why_it_matters: Early gradients and optimizer statistics can be unstable, especially in large-batch or transformer training, so abrupt full-size updates may damage optimization.

attrs.definition: Minimum work to transport mass from one distribution to another. A true metric
attrs.name: Wasserstein distance

attrs.definition: Bits embedded in audio, survive re-encode.
attrs.name: Watermark

attrs.definition: Classic scalable-oversight benchmark AARs outperformed humans on
attrs.folk_definition: "Training a stronger model with a weaker supervisor"
attrs.name: Weak-to-strong training

attrs.definition: Word Embedding Association Test; co-occurrence-based bias probe
attrs.name: WEAT

attrs.definition: 812 tasks across 4 self-hosted apps; gym-style evaluation
attrs.name: WebArena

attrs.definition: ServiceNow's regraded WebArena with Hard subset
attrs.name: WebArena-Verified

attrs.definition: W3C-standardized browser GPU API; Chrome/Safari 2026
attrs.name: WebGPU

attrs.definition: MLC-LLM project; Apache 2.0; OpenAI-compatible JS
attrs.name: WebLLM

attrs.confusion: Not every parameter is called a weight; biases, embeddings, and normalization scales are parameters too.
attrs.definition: A trainable coefficient in a model transformation. Weights are usually organized into tensors, and optimization adjusts them to reduce the training objective.
attrs.folk_definition: A learned number inside a model.
attrs.name: Weight

attrs.confusion: Decoupled weight decay is equivalent to an L2 loss penalty for some simple optimizers, but not generally for adaptive optimizers such as Adam.
attrs.definition: An update rule that reduces selected parameter magnitudes over training, often by multiplying weights by a shrinkage factor separate from the gradient update.
attrs.folk_definition: Regularization that shrinks weights during optimization.
attrs.name: Weight Decay
attrs.why_it_matters: It can improve generalization, but the useful coefficient and excluded parameter groups depend on model, optimizer, schedule, and data.

attrs.definition: Normalize conv weights instead of activations; kills droplet artifacts.
attrs.name: Weight demodulation

attrs.definition: The strategy for choosing initial weight values that determines whether a network can train at all
attrs.name: Weight initialization

attrs.definition: A matrix W of shape (current_layer_neurons, previous_layer_neurons) containing learnable connection strengths
attrs.name: Weight matrix

attrs.definition: Using the same matrix for input token embeddings and the output projection head -- saves 38M params in GPT-2
attrs.name: Weight tying

attrs.definition: Setting model.lm_head.weight = model.tok_embed.weight so the head and embedding share storage; the head is not in the file because of this
attrs.name: Weight tying alias

attrs.definition: Neighbors weighted inversely by distance. Closer neighbors have more influence on the prediction
attrs.name: Weighted KNN

attrs.definition: (S+D+I)/N at word level.
attrs.name: WER

attrs.definition: Replace BCE with Earth-Mover distance + gradient penalty; smoother gradient.
attrs.name: WGAN

attrs.definition: Policy that doesn't evict running GPU jobs
attrs.name: WhenEmpty + 1h

attrs.definition: large-v3 encoder + 4-layer decoder; 8× faster decoding.
attrs.name: Whisper-turbo

attrs.definition: VAD + Whisper + wav2vec alignment + diarization.
attrs.name: WhisperX

attrs.definition: A confidence interval for pass/fail rates that works correctly even with small sample sizes or extreme proportions
attrs.name: Wilson interval

attrs.definition: Point-wise multiplier that tapers the frame edges to zero.
attrs.name: Window

attrs.definition: Spatial self-attention restricted to small windows for speed; global attention added periodically
attrs.name: Window attention

attrs.definition: A tapering function (Hann, Hamming, Blackman) applied before DFT to reduce spectral leakage
attrs.name: Window function

attrs.definition: Workshop on Multi-Agent Coordination; community focal point.
attrs.name: WMAC

attrs.definition: April 2026 community focal point for multi-agent coordination.
attrs.name: WMAC 2026

attrs.definition: 4,157 MCQ questions across bio/cyber/chem in the yellow zone
attrs.name: WMDP

attrs.definition: A dense, low-dim (typically 100-300) representation learned from context.
attrs.name: Word embedding

attrs.definition: 2013 model that learned word vectors by predicting context words; proved vector arithmetic encodes meaning
attrs.name: Word2Vec

attrs.definition: Like BPE but merges maximize the likelihood ratio count(AB)/(count(A)count(B)) instead of raw frequency
attrs.name: WordPiece

attrs.definition: Engineered surfaces around the model that make work reliable
attrs.name: Workbench

attrs.definition: A pass over the seven surfaces that flags missing pieces before work begins
attrs.name: Workbench audit

attrs.definition: Portable harness that runs the comparison on your codebase
attrs.name: Workbench benchmark

attrs.definition: A versioned directory carrying all seven surfaces
attrs.name: Workbench pack

attrs.definition: A focused agent invoked by the supervisor with narrow scope and its own context window.
attrs.name: Worker

attrs.definition: Engineer-owned graph of LLM and tool calls
attrs.name: Workflow

attrs.definition: Interactive / semi / batch routing decision
attrs.name: Workload triage

attrs.confusion: A worktree isolates checked-out files, not every process, port, cache, database, or secret on the machine.
attrs.definition: In Git, a working directory attached to a repository and branch or commit, with shared object storage but its own checked-out files and index.
attrs.in_practice: Give each coding agent a named feature branch and exact worktree path, then review and integrate patches through normal Git history.
attrs.name: Worktree
attrs.why_it_matters: Separate worktrees let people and agents work concurrently without constantly switching or overwriting one checkout.

attrs.definition: A model that predicts future observations given state and action
attrs.name: World model

attrs.definition: Number of processes in the group; the group is the unit collectives operate on
attrs.name: World size

attrs.definition: Injected content includes instructions to propagate
attrs.name: Worming

attrs.definition: A feature selection approach that evaluates feature subsets by training a model and using its performance as the selection criterion
attrs.name: Wrapper method

attrs.definition: Carries Bearer error=... directives that drive client recovery
attrs.name: WWW-Authenticate

attrs.definition: Schema annotation that mirrors a primitive argument into Streamable HTTP metadata
attrs.name: x-mcp-header

attrs.definition: Var(w) = 2/(fan_in + fan_out), designed to preserve variance through sigmoid and tanh activations
attrs.name: Xavier/Glorot init

attrs.definition: Gradient boosting with regularization, second-order optimization, and systems-level speed tricks
attrs.name: XGBoost

attrs.definition: Accelerated Linear Algebra -- a compiler that fuses operations and generates optimized GPU/TPU kernels from a computation graph
attrs.name: XLA

attrs.definition: 100-language RoBERTa pretrained on CommonCrawl.
attrs.name: XLM-R

attrs.definition: Proof that single-layer networks cannot learn non-linearly-separable functions
attrs.name: XOR problem

attrs.definition: Cross-Prompt Injection Attack filter; bypassed by EchoLeak
attrs.name: XPIA

attrs.definition: Benchmark for over-refusal regression
attrs.name: XSTest

attrs.definition: Per-dimension interpolation+extrapolation that preserves attention entropy.
attrs.name: YaRN

attrs.definition: Proximate knowledge adjacent to harmful capability without being a synthesis recipe
attrs.name: Yellow zone

attrs.definition: (x - mean) / std, measuring how far a point is from the center in units of standard deviation
attrs.name: Z-score

attrs.definition: Zero Redundancy Optimizer with 3 stages: shard optimizer (Stage 1), + gradients (Stage 2), + parameters (Stage 3)
attrs.name: ZeRO

attrs.definition: Each rank holds 1/N of fp32 master + Adam moments
attrs.name: ZeRO-1

attrs.definition: Each rank also drops the non-shard gradients after reduce_scatter
attrs.name: ZeRO-2

attrs.definition: Each rank holds 1/N of fp16 params; allgather per layer in forward
attrs.name: ZeRO-3

attrs.definition: Splits backward into B (input gradient) and W (weight gradient); almost fully tightens the pipeline
attrs.name: Zero Bubble

attrs.definition: Attack triggers automatically during agent operation; user does nothing
attrs.name: Zero-click

attrs.definition: 1×1 conv initialized to zero; ControlNet starts as no-op.
attrs.name: Zero convolution

attrs.definition: Resetting all parameter gradients to zero before computing the next batch's gradients
attrs.name: Zero grad

attrs.confusion: Zero-shot does not mean the model had no relevant pretraining, instruction tuning, tools, or retrieved context.
attrs.definition: Performing a task from instructions or task framing without including task-specific demonstrations in the immediate input.
attrs.folk_definition: Asking for a task without examples in the current prompt.
attrs.name: Zero-Shot

attrs.definition: Verbalize labels as hypotheses, pick max entailment.
attrs.name: Zero-shot classification

attrs.definition: Pretrained model + speaker embedding; no training.
attrs.name: Zero-shot clone

attrs.definition: Appending a reasoning trigger phrase to a prompt without any examples, relying on the model's latent reasoning capability
attrs.name: Zero-shot CoT

attrs.confusion: Zero trust does not mean trusting nothing or blocking all automation. It means making trust decisions explicit, scoped, and continuously verifiable.
attrs.definition: A security model that grants no implicit trust from network location or asset ownership and instead evaluates each access request against identity, device, resource, policy, and current context.
attrs.in_practice: Authenticate every actor and workload, authorize each resource action, issue short-lived credentials, segment access, and continuously record and reevaluate policy-relevant signals.
attrs.name: Zero Trust
attrs.why_it_matters: AI tools and agents span local files, cloud services, models, and external content, so a trusted internal network is too broad a basis for authority.

attrs.definition: Classical offer-generator that concedes based on risk limits.
attrs.name: Zeuthen strategy

attrs.definition: TS runtime schema for provider output validation
attrs.name: Zod schema

attrs.definition: Overlap between buyer's max and seller's min. Offers outside it cannot close.
attrs.name: ZOPA

attrs.hook: Your tools shape your thinking. Set them up once, set them up right.
attrs.title: Dev Environment

attrs.hook: Version control is not optional. Every experiment, every model, every lesson you build here gets tracked.
attrs.title: Git & Collaboration

attrs.hook: Training on CPU is fine for learning. Training for real needs a GPU.
attrs.title: GPU Setup & Cloud

attrs.hook: Every AI API works the same way: send a request, get a response. The details change, the pattern doesn't.
attrs.title: APIs & Keys

attrs.hook: Notebooks are the lab bench of AI engineering. You prototype here, then move what works into production.
attrs.title: Jupyter Notebooks

attrs.hook: Dependency hell is real. Virtual environments are the cure.
attrs.title: Python Environments

attrs.hook: Containers make "works on my machine" a thing of the past.
attrs.title: Docker for AI

attrs.hook: Your editor is your co-pilot. Configure it once so it stays out of your way and starts pulling its weight.
attrs.title: Editor Setup

attrs.hook: Data is the fuel. How you manage it determines how fast you go.
attrs.title: Data Management

attrs.hook: The terminal is where AI engineers live. Get comfortable here.
attrs.title: Terminal & Shell

attrs.hook: Most AI runs on Linux. You need to know enough to not be stuck.
attrs.title: Linux for AI

attrs.hook: The worst AI bugs don't crash. They train silently on garbage and report a beautiful loss curve.
attrs.title: Debugging and Profiling

attrs.hook: Every AI model is just matrix math wearing a fancy hat.
attrs.title: Linear Algebra Intuition

attrs.hook: Every neural network is just matrix multiplication with extra steps.
attrs.title: Vectors, Matrices & Operations

attrs.hook: A matrix is a machine that reshapes space. Learn what it does to every point, and you understand the whole transformation.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1, Lessons 01-02 (Linear Algebra Intuition, Vectors & Matrices Operations)
attrs.title: Matrix Transformations

attrs.hook: Derivatives tell you which way is downhill. That is all a neural network needs to learn.
attrs.title: Calculus for Machine Learning

attrs.hook: The chain rule is the engine behind every neural network that learns.
attrs.title: Chain Rule & Automatic Differentiation

attrs.hook: Probability is the language AI uses to express uncertainty.
attrs.title: Probability and Distributions

attrs.hook: Probability is about what you expect. Bayes' theorem is about what you learn.
attrs.title: Bayes' Theorem

attrs.hook: Training a neural network is nothing more than finding the bottom of a valley.
attrs.title: Optimization

attrs.hook: Information theory measures surprise. Loss functions are built on it.
attrs.title: Information Theory

attrs.hook: High-dimensional data has structure. You find it by looking from the right angle.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1, Lessons 01 (Linear Algebra Intuition), 02 (Vectors, Matrices & Operations), 03 (Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors), 06 (Probability & Distributions)
attrs.title: Dimensionality Reduction

attrs.hook: SVD is the Swiss Army knife of linear algebra. Every matrix has one. Every data scientist needs one.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1, Lessons 01 (Linear Algebra Intuition), 02 (Vectors & Matrices Operations), 03 (Matrix Transformations)
attrs.title: Singular Value Decomposition

attrs.hook: Tensors are the common language between data and deep learning. Every image, every sentence, every gradient flows through them.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1, Lessons 01 (Linear Algebra Intuition), 02 (Vectors, Matrices & Operations)
attrs.title: Tensor Operations

attrs.hook: Floating point is a leaky abstraction. It will bite you during training, and you will not see it coming.
attrs.title: Numerical Stability

attrs.hook: Your distance function defines what "similar" means. Choose wrong and everything downstream breaks.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1, Lessons 01 (Linear Algebra Intuition), 02 (Vectors, Matrices & Operations)
attrs.title: Norms and Distances

attrs.hook: Statistics is how you know if your model actually works or just got lucky.
attrs.title: Statistics for Machine Learning

attrs.hook: Sampling is how AI explores the space of possibilities.
attrs.title: Sampling Methods

attrs.hook: Solving Ax = b is the oldest problem in mathematics that still runs your neural network.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1, Lessons 01 (Linear Algebra Intuition), 02 (Vectors & Matrices), 03 (Matrix Transformations)
attrs.title: Linear Systems

attrs.hook: Convex problems have one valley. Neural networks have millions. Knowing the difference matters.
attrs.title: Convex Optimization

attrs.hook: The square root of -1 is not imaginary. It is the key to rotations, frequencies, and half of signal processing.
attrs.title: Complex Numbers for AI

attrs.hook: Every signal is a sum of sine waves. The Fourier transform tells you which ones.
attrs.title: The Fourier Transform

attrs.hook: Graphs are the data structure of relationships. If your data has connections, you need graph theory.
attrs.title: Graph Theory for Machine Learning

attrs.hook: Randomness with structure. The math behind random walks, Markov chains, and diffusion models.
attrs.title: Stochastic Processes

attrs.hook: Machine learning is teaching computers to find patterns in data instead of writing rules by hand.
attrs.title: What Is Machine Learning

attrs.hook: Linear regression draws the best straight line through your data. It is the "hello world" of machine learning.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1 (Linear Algebra, Calculus, Optimization), Phase 2 Lesson 1
attrs.title: Linear Regression

attrs.hook: Logistic regression bends a straight line into an S-curve to answer yes-or-no questions with probabilities.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 2 Lesson 1-2 (What Is ML, Linear Regression)
attrs.title: Logistic Regression

attrs.hook: A decision tree is just a flowchart. But a forest of them is one of the most powerful tools in ML.
attrs.title: Decision Trees and Random Forests

attrs.hook: Find the widest street between two classes. That is the entire idea.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1 (Lessons 08 Optimization, 14 Norms and Distances, 18 Convex Optimization)
attrs.title: Support Vector Machines

attrs.hook: Store everything. Predict by looking at your neighbors. The simplest algorithm that actually works.
attrs.title: K-Nearest Neighbors and Distances

attrs.hook: No labels, no teacher. The algorithm finds structure on its own.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1 (Norms & Distances, Probability & Distributions), Phase 2 Lessons 1-6
attrs.title: Unsupervised Learning

attrs.hook: A good feature is worth a thousand data points.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1 (Statistics for ML, Linear Algebra), Phase 2 Lessons 1-7
attrs.title: Feature Engineering & Selection

attrs.hook: A model is only as good as the way you measure it.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 1 (Probability & Distributions, Statistics for ML), Phase 2 Lessons 1-8
attrs.title: Model Evaluation

attrs.hook: Every model error comes from one of three sources: bias, variance, or noise. You can only control the first two.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 2, Lessons 01-09 (ML basics, regression, classification, evaluation)
attrs.title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff

attrs.hook: A group of weak learners, combined correctly, becomes a strong learner. This is not a metaphor. It is a theorem.
attrs.title: Ensemble Methods

attrs.hook: Hyperparameters are the knobs you turn before training starts. Turning them well is the difference between a mediocre model and a great one.
attrs.title: Hyperparameter Tuning

attrs.hook: A model is not a product. A pipeline is. The pipeline is everything from raw data to deployed prediction, and every step must be reproducible.
attrs.title: ML Pipelines

attrs.hook: The "naive" assumption is wrong, and it works anyway. That's the beauty of it.
attrs.title: Naive Bayes

attrs.hook: Past performance does predict future results -- if you check for stationarity first.
attrs.title: Time Series Fundamentals

attrs.hook: Normal is easy to define. Abnormal is whatever doesn't fit.
attrs.title: Anomaly Detection

attrs.hook: When 99% of your data is "normal," accuracy is a lie.
attrs.title: Handling Imbalanced Data

attrs.hook: More features is not better. The right features is better.
attrs.title: Feature Selection

attrs.hook: The perceptron is the atom of neural networks. Split it open and you find weights, a bias, and a decision.
attrs.title: The Perceptron

attrs.hook: One neuron draws a line. Stack them, and you can draw anything.
attrs.title: Multi-Layer Networks and Forward Pass

attrs.hook: Backpropagation is the algorithm that makes learning possible. Without it, neural networks are just expensive random number generators.
attrs.title: Backpropagation from Scratch

attrs.hook: Without nonlinearity, your 100-layer network is a fancy matrix multiply. Activations are the gates that let neural networks think in curves.
attrs.title: Activation Functions

attrs.hook: Your network makes a prediction. The ground truth says otherwise. How wrong is it? That number is the loss. Pick the wrong loss function and your model optimizes for the wrong thing entirely.
attrs.title: Loss Functions

attrs.hook: Gradient descent tells you which direction to move. It says nothing about how far or how fast. SGD is a compass. Adam is GPS with traffic data.
attrs.title: Optimizers

attrs.hook: Your model gets 99% on training data and 60% on test data. It memorized instead of learning. Regularization is the tax you impose on complexity to force generalization.
attrs.title: Regularization

attrs.hook: Initialize wrong and training never starts. Initialize right and 50 layers train as smoothly as 3.
attrs.title: Weight Initialization and Training Stability

attrs.hook: The learning rate is the single most important hyperparameter. Not the architecture. Not the dataset size. Not the activation function. The learning rate. If you tune nothing else, tune this.
attrs.title: Learning Rate Schedules and Warmup

attrs.hook: You have built neurons, layers, networks, backprop, activations, loss functions, optimizers, regularization, initialization, and LR schedules. All as separate pieces. Now wire them together into a framework. Not PyTorch. Not TensorFlow. Yours.
attrs.title: Build Your Own Mini Framework

attrs.hook: You built the engine from pistons and crankshafts. Now learn the one everyone actually drives.
attrs.title: Introduction to PyTorch

attrs.hook: PyTorch mutates tensors. TensorFlow builds graphs. JAX compiles pure functions. That last one changes how you think about deep learning.
attrs.title: Introduction to JAX

attrs.hook: Your network compiled. It ran. It produced a number. The number is wrong and nothing crashed. Welcome to the hardest kind of debugging -- the kind where there is no error message.
attrs.prereq_raw: Phase 03 Lessons 01-10 (especially backpropagation, loss functions, optimizers)
attrs.title: Debugging Neural Networks

attrs.hook: An image is a tensor of light samples. Every vision model you will ever use starts from this one fact.

attrs.hook: A convolution is a tiny dense layer you slide across an image, sharing the same weights at every location.
